title: adaptive-session-graceful-degradation-and-client-merge-for-hosted-streams
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Summary: Multiple enterprise customers reported truncated or duplicated partial responses when using Hosted API streaming (SSE) during sustained long outputs or transient infra events. Symptoms: mid-stream abrupt termination with no final sentinel, client SDK resume failing to rehydrate last tokens, and in a subset of cases duplicate tail tokens after reconnect. Impact: customer-facing data loss or UI corruption for chat and code-generation features; several high-severity escalations opened by CS. Scope: observed across Hosted and some Dedicated edge placements; Private installs have not reported identical failure modes but may be vulnerable to same logic paths. Root cause hypothesis: when autoscaler and edge LB rebalances active nodes, the ephemeral session mapping (edge -> backend worker) can be replaced before the final flush and sentinel emission; ephemeral worker restarts can drop last KV cache flush and the resume handshake in the SDK relies on a final token marker that is not emitted for a small class of completion paths. Additionally, a race in the stream-handoff logic can result in the resumed session being stitched to a worker that has re-emitted an overlapping token sequence, causing visible duplication. Goals: 1) Implement server-side adaptive graceful-degradation that keeps a short-lived deferral window on autoscaler-triggered reassignments for active SSE sessions. 2) Improve the resume handshake/protocol to include a deterministic finalization nonce and sequence checksum so clients can detect exact tail continuity or request server-side backfill. 3) Provide a client-side merge strategy in SDKs that can safely reconcile overlapping partials without user-visible duplication. Deliverables: - runtime: sticky-session grace period + controlled drain instead of immediate kill on scale-down - protocol: add finality nonce + rolling sequence checksum in SSE metadata - sdk: merge heuristics that prefer server-side backfill when checksum mismatch is detected - observability: add per-session sequence-gap metric, finality nonce presence rate, and customer-impact dashboard - runbook: customer-facing mitigation steps and escalation templates Trade-offs and considerations: - Extending drain windows increases resource hold time under autoscaling (cost), but for customer sessions this is acceptable for a P0 escalated path. We will make this configurable by tenant and default to short durations (5s) while adding a tuning knob in Dedicated. - Full server-side reassembly/backfill is more complex (stateful buffering) and is scheduled as follow-up if checksum/backfill handshake shows high-demand. Current plan favors protocol determinism + client merge to reduce complexity upfront.
comments: 2025-02-08 - Aisha Patel: Triage call with CS and oncall. Customer A (enterprise chat) reproduced with a long completion (>=6k tokens). Collected SDK logs and last-server receipts. Escalated to eng oncall.

2025-02-09 - Marco Ruiz: Reproduced locally with stress harness by simulating abrupt worker stop during final flush. Observed missing final sentinel and duplicate last 20 tokens after reconnect in ~3% of runs.

2025-02-10 - Lina Cho (SRE): Found correlation between autoscaler preemption events and stream termination in edge logs. Hooked a debug flag to preserve connection context during drain for test cluster.

2025-02-11 - Marco Ruiz: Prototype implemented: 'graceful drain' window (configurable 5s) prevents immediate session handoff. Early tests reduced duplicates to <0.1% but increased median worker hold time by 3.2%.
2025-02-12 - Design review: Decided to add finality nonce and rolling sequence checksum as minimal required protocol metadata. PM approves customer-visible behavior change and rollback plan.

2025-02-13 - QA: Integration tests added to sdk-resilience suite. Added fuzz test to simulate LBs dropping connections mid-chunk. Found edge-case where partial JSON fragments could still appear malformed — added chunk-boundary sanity checks.
2025-02-14 - Marco Ruiz: Opened PR for runtime changes and feature flag gating: runtime PR #4512. Added metrics to staging: sse.session.finality_missing and sse.session.sequence_gap_count.
2025-02-15 - Security review kickoff: security flagged the need to ensure finality nonce cannot be used for session fixation attacks; applying HMAC using request-specific nonce per session.

2025-02-18 - Aisha Patel: Customer comms drafted and shared with Support for canary outreach to top affected customers. Plan: deploy feature-flagged change to 5% of traffic, validate metrics, then ramp.
2025-02-18 - Marco Ruiz: QA green on staging. Scheduling canary deployment and post-deploy smoke tests.
